title: Identity and Infrastructure Governance: How to Close the Gaps in Your Cloud Environment
summary: Learn how identity and infrastructure governance helps secure Entra apps, reduce cloud risk, prevent outages, and strengthen accountability. Read more.
body_markdown:
Entra applications, identities, and cloud configurations are the invisible foundation of modern work, and for most organizations, they've become a blind spot.


For years, governance has focused on the places people


collaborate


most: Teams, SharePoint, documents, and email. That focus made sense — this is where content lives, and where the risk is most visible.


But modern business environments


run on


much more than files and folders. They run on the **Entra applications, identities, and cloud configurations** underneath them. These can be spun up quickly, often lack clear ownership, and quietly drift over time — creating cost, risk, and outages that native tools often don't catch.


That underlying layer has become a blind spot, and AvePoint is addressing it through


a unified


governance framework.


*Enterprise applications are just the newest part of AvePoint’s unified security posture and governance framework*


## The Problem: Sprawl You Can't See, Own, or Trust


Ask most cloud architects how many Entra applications and app registrations live in their Microsoft Entra tenant, and you'll get an estimate — not a precise count. Across industries, it is common to see tenants with **thousands, and in some cases tens of thousands, of Entra applications** . And this isn't just clutter: Every ungoverned app is a live entry point, which means that sprawl at this scale quietly becomes one of the **largest unmanaged attack surfaces** in your environment.


Each one represents a potential entry point into your environment. Each one also raises questions that are surprisingly hard to answer:


- How many orphaned apps still have standing access?
- Who should be responsible for them?
- Does this app have more privilege than it should?
- Who approved this access, and can we prove it to an auditor?


Expired secrets and certificates are among the most common causes of identity-related outages, the kind that take down a business-critical service without warning. Meanwhile, ownership is unclear, permissions change silently, and attestation is handled through manual spreadsheets and time-intensive reviews. Increasingly, auditors are also requiring organizations to prove who has access, why that access exists, and whether it's still justified.


Native tooling provides point-in-time visibility. What it doesn't give you is accountability: a durable owner, a defined lifecycle, and a system of record that stays current as your environment evolves.


*Screenshot of AvePoint’s Entra Application governance*


## The Shift From Visibility to Accountability


Visibility tells you what exists; governance makes someone responsible for it.


That's the foundation of what Entra Application Governance: a control plane for the apps, resources, and configurations your business runs on, so every high-value asset has an owner, a purpose, and a way back to a known-good state.


Designed to transform a sprawling, unowned inventory of Entra applications into accountable, well-governed assets, it enables:


- **Discovery & inventory.** Gain full visibility into every Entra application and app registration in your tenant.
- **Ownership & accountability.** Assign, track, and attest ownership so every app has a responsible business owner — engaging the business, not just IT.
- **Lifecycle governance.** Renewals, attestation, and delegated administration keep the environment clean and current, replacing manual reviews with structured workflows.
- **Risk visibility.** Surface orphaned apps, expiring credentials, and unmanaged service principals before they become exposures.


The result: fewer surprise outages from expired secrets, a defensible answer when auditors come calling, and a real reduction in the hidden carrying costs of ungoverned growth.


This matters even more as AI agents and workload identities proliferate. Agents can spin up their own app registrations, accelerating sprawl — and each is a non-human identity that needs the same discipline as a human one: a verified human owner, clear metadata, and continuous compliance. Extending ownership and accountability to these identities is what keeps an AI-ready foundation trustworthy as it scales.


## One Governance Strategy for All Your Data


Entra applications are the starting point, not the whole story. Governing your foundation requires governance across applications, infrastructure, and the configurations that connect them.


Entra Application Governance is the first step in a broader, connected approach to identity and infrastructure governance, alongside upcoming capabilities:


- With Azure resource group governance, the same ownership and lifecycle discipline can be extended to Azure environments, helping turn wasteful, unowned spend into optimized, accountable resources.
- With baselines management, organizations can define known-good configurations, detect drift before it becomes an incident, and maintain continuous alignment through change tracking and rollback capabilities.


Together, these capabilities support a simple objective: **keep every app, resource, and configuration owned, current, and in a known-good state,** so you can prevent what you can, recover what you can't, and give your business an AI-ready foundation it can trust.


## Govern With Confidence


The apps and identities underneath your business aren't going to slow down. But sprawl doesn't have to mean risk. With ownership, lifecycle, and drift control across your cloud estate, you can scale innovation without scaling exposure.
